Speaking as someone who's been here since before this shit hit the fan, can somebody explain to me in a calm and rational manner what all the fuss is about, and why it's so particularly bad and so personal?

To me the banning of /r/fatpeoplehate just looked like a straightforward corporate image management decision because the subreddit had become a particularly public embarrassment. Somewhat spineless, I grant you, but not unprecedented, not atypical for the American media-corporate world, and certainly not nearly as bad as the political propaganda and manipulation and gaming of public opinion that goes on at reddit (it'll increasingly happen here too as voat grows bigger; heck, some subverses have already been banned). So what makes the latest Pao/FatPeopleHate thing so different as to trigger this extreme response?

A few things. She's ordered her admins to remove posts badmouthing her. It's like a post-removal version of a shadowban, where logged-in users can still see them, but lurkers cannot. Basically punching up her own image to those who don't already know and hate her.

When /r/fatpeoplehate was removed, they said they were removing it because of a harassment campaign it had started, and that any subs that were banned were being 'banned for behavior, not ideas.' However, all of the community's attempts to create a replacement sub saw them pretty much instabanned. Sounds a lot like banning for ideas to me.

Most recently, Reddit fired the community outreach... person (also a mod) of /r/IAMA. She was one of the few popular mods left, and was responsible (at least in part) for a great deal of the AMAs by celebrities, scientists, politicians, and other famous people who probably wouldn't otherwise use Reddit. They've been exceedingly silent about the reason she was fired, and in fact won't even cop to the fact that they fired her, instead saying they 'parted ways'. She was one of the few mods still operating out of New York, and that may or may not have been a major factor in what happened (wanting to keep all their employees close together, I guess?).

Also, the general attitude they have about the blackout. That 'oh, we just need to weather the storm and then the pleb rabble will calm down', rather than thinking 'Wow, we really pissed off our userbase. Maybe we should do something to fix it'

Personally, it wasn't any one reason that caused me to make the switch, it was a combination of factors. SJW brigading and nepotism, censorship, and the general way that the new regime has been treating the userbase like their bitches... Those're what made me leave.
